findings.claim: Reaction time "is Required Practical 7 in the AQA specification" (also in the collapsible heading "Required Practical 7: Measuring Reaction Time").
findings.truth: For this qualification the reaction-time investigation is required practical activity 6; activity 7 is measuring population size with quadrats and a transect. The board is also named in student-facing text.
findings.evidence: spec 8464 line 2622: 'Required practical activity 6: plan and carry out an investigation into the effect of a factor on human reaction time'; line 3774: activity 7 is population size. (Activity 7 is the reaction-time number in the separate Biology spec, which is where this wording came from.)

findings.claim: "Reflex actions do not involve the conscious part of the brain - they are coordinated by the spinal cord."
findings.truth: Some reflexes are coordinated in the brain, not the spinal cord. The lesson's own examples (pupil constricting, blinking) are cranial reflexes. The spec only says reflexes do not involve the conscious part of the brain.
findings.evidence: spec 8464 4.5.2: 'Reflex actions are automatic and rapid; they do not involve the conscious part of the brain.' The spec never says reflexes are coordinated only by the spinal cord.

findings.claim: "For AQA Trilogy questions on this topic..."
findings.truth: House rule: never name the exam board in student-facing text.
findings.evidence: house rule (board-neutral phrasing).

findings.claim: Ruler-drop method: "One person holds a ruler vertically at the 0 cm mark. A second person places their thumb and finger around the ruler at the 0 mark..."
findings.truth: Both people cannot be at the 0 cm mark. The holder holds the top of the ruler; the catcher's fingers sit at the 0 cm mark.
findings.evidence: standard method for the reaction-time required practical.

findings.claim: The <div class="higher-only"> opened before "Hormone Interactions - Negative Feedback" is never closed before the Contraception section; the whole of contraception (plus its key fact) sits inside the Higher-only wrapper, which css/style.css hides completely for Foundation students.
findings.truth: Contraception is not Higher-tier content: it carries no HT marker and is examined at both tiers. Only the hormone-interaction section and the infertility/IVF section are HT only. The wrapper must close after the Higher-tier feedback key fact, and the surplus closing div at the end of the field must go.
findings.evidence: spec 8464 4.5.3.4 Contraception has no '(HT only)' marker, unlike 4.5.3.3's interactions statements and 4.5.3.5 'The use of hormones to treat infertility (HT only)'. css/style.css:5102 'body.tier-foundation .higher-only { display: none !important; }'.

findings.claim: Fill question "In IVF, eggs are fertilised with sperm in a _____ dish" marks only option 1 ('laboratory') correct, but option 0 is 'petri'.
findings.truth: A Petri dish is where IVF fertilisation happens, so a student who picks 'petri' gives a correct answer and is marked wrong. The distractor must be changed.

findings.claim: Lessons 9-13 teach the brain, the eye, thermoregulation, the kidney and ADH, plant hormones, DNA structure and protein synthesis, cloning, trophic levels and biomass efficiency, decay rate, food security and biotechnology, all inside a unit built on the Combined Science (Trilogy) specification.
findings.truth: None of this content is on the Combined Science specification. Every one of those topics is flagged '(biology only)' in the separate Biology specification, i.e. separate-science-only. The five lessons also pull their diagrams from the separate-sciences R2 folder, so they look like a straight port. Options for Tom: (a) move lessons 9-13 into the separate-sciences subject and drop them here, (b) keep them but relabel them plainly as extension material that is not on this paper, (c) leave as-is and accept that a third of the unit is off-spec. Recommendation: (b) as a stop-gap this week, (a) properly, because the free-tier/bespoke rule is that content must match the qualification.
findings.evidence: spec 8461 headings: 4.5.2.2 The brain (biology only); 4.5.2.3 The eye (biology only); 4.5.2.4 Control of body temperature (biology only); 4.5.3.3 Maintaining water and nitrogen balance (biology only); 4.6.1.5 DNA structure (biology only); 4.7.4 Trophic levels (biology only); 4.7.5 Food production (biology only). None of these sections exists in spec 8464. Diagram URLs in L9-L13 all point at r2.dev/separate-sciences/biology-separate/.

findings.claim: Lessons 9, 10, 11, 12 and 13 carry the slugs lesson-03, lesson-04, lesson-05, lesson-06 and lesson-07 - the same slugs as lessons 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 in the same unit.
findings.truth: Student state is keyed on unit slug + lesson slug, so lesson 9 shares its visited flag and its knowledge-check store with lesson 3, and so on down the pairs. Finishing lesson 3 marks lesson 9 as visited and the two lessons overwrite each other's knowledge-check scores. The fix is a database change (renumber lessons 9-13 to lesson-09..lesson-13), not a text edit, and it should be done alongside whatever is decided for F12 - if those five lessons move out, the clash goes with them.
findings.evidence: js/main.js:198 markVisited(unitSlug, lessonSlug) and js/main.js:1876 storageKey = 'studyvault-kc-' + unit + '/' + lesson, both fed from document.body.dataset.lesson = lesson.slug (js/lesson-loader.js:355).

findings.evidence: spec 8461 4.5.2.2: '(HT only) Students should be able to explain some of the difficulties of investigating brain function...' and '(HT only) Neuroscientists have been able to map the regions of the brain...'.

findings.claim: The trophic-level knowledge checks use the option strings 'Level 1', 'Level 2', 'Level 3', 'Level 4'.
findings.truth: These are correct science (the specification numbers trophic levels exactly this way) but they collide word for word with the house validator's banned band-name strings 'Level 1'..'Level 9'. If the validator is a plain substring check it will reject this unit on apply even though nothing is wrong. Worth making that check context-aware rather than editing correct content.

findings.claim: The figure carries placeholder text: alt "Generated diagram for Trophic Levels and Transfer of Biomass" and the same string as a visible <figcaption>.
findings.truth: Students see the placeholder caption under the diagram. Diagrams are outside this check's remit, so it is recorded rather than edited.

findings.claim: Collapsible headed "Required Practical: Investigating the Effect of Temperature on Decay".
findings.truth: This qualification has no required practical on the rate of decay. In the separate Biology specification it is activity 10, and the method described (milk, lipase, sodium carbonate, phenolphthalein, time to lose the pink colour) is right for it. The 'Required Practical' label is dropped so the claim is true whichever subject the lesson ends up in.
findings.evidence: spec 8461 line 4391: 'Required practical activity 10: investigate the effect of temperature on the rate of decay of fresh milk by measuring pH change.' No equivalent in spec 8464.

findings.claim: "Darwin called this 'survival of the fittest.'"
findings.truth: The phrase was coined by Herbert Spencer in 1864; Darwin adopted it from the fifth edition of On the Origin of Species onwards. The sentence is therefore defensible rather than false, so it is recorded, not corrected.
findings.evidence: settled fact; attribution is shared, so no edit.

findings.claim: The protein-synthesis section teaches transcription, translation, mRNA and ribosomes in detail, and a knowledge check tests the name 'transcription'.
findings.truth: The separate Biology specification says students are not expected to know the structure of mRNA; none of it is on the Combined Science specification. The science is correct, so this is scope, not error - it rolls up into F12.
findings.evidence: spec 8461 4.6.1.5: '(HT only) Students are not expected to know or understand the structure of mRNA, tRNA, or the detailed structure of amino acids or proteins.'

findings.claim: Lesson 4 teaches nucleotides, the four bases and complementary base pairing, and a knowledge check tests A-T pairing.
findings.truth: On this qualification DNA is only 'a polymer made up of two strands forming a double helix'; base pairing is separate-science content and Higher tier there. Correct science taught beyond the specification, so it is recorded, not edited.
findings.evidence: spec 8464 4.6.1.3 (no bases listed); spec 8461 4.6.1.5 'DNA structure (biology only)' with '(HT only) In the complementary strands a C is always linked to a G...'.

findings.claim: Lesson 9's description is 101 characters and lesson 13's is exactly 100.
findings.truth: The house limit is under 100 characters, so both rows would fail the validator. Shortened without losing meaning.
findings.evidence: house validator limit; measured lengths 101 and 100.

summary: Thirteen lessons checked. The science is largely sound and every calculation recomputes (Punnett squares, quadrat estimates, biomass efficiencies, percentage change, amino acids from bases). The two structural problems are bigger than the text errors: lessons 9-13 are separate-science Biology content sitting in a Combined Science unit, and those same five lessons duplicate the slugs of lessons 3-7, which makes their visited flags and knowledge-check scores collide. Of the text errors, the worst are a Higher-only wrapper in lesson 3 that hides the whole contraception section from Foundation students, a wrong required-practical number in lesson 1, and a mangled flashcard in lesson 5.
